Hyperventilation involves rapid breathing that expels more carbon dioxide than normal from the lungs.  
This reduces the partial pressure of CO₂ in the blood.  
Less CO₂ means less carbonic acid forms in the blood, which in turn means fewer hydrogen ions (H⁺), so blood pH rises (respiratory alkalosis).  
Thus, partial pressure of CO₂ decreases and hydrogen ion concentration decreases.
